questions.stem: The general formula of the alkanes is
questions.explanation: Alkanes are saturated, so each carbon forms four single bonds and the chain carries the maximum number of hydrogen atoms. Every carbon in the chain contributes two hydrogens, with two extra at the ends, giving CnH2n+2. Checking with propane, n = 3 gives C3H8.

distractorRationale.a: CnH2n is the general formula of the alkenes, which contain one double bond
distractorRationale.c: CnH2n-2 is the general formula of the alkynes, which contain a triple bond
distractorRationale.d: CnH2n+1OH is the general formula of the alkanols

questions.stem: How many structural isomers has butane, C4H10?
questions.explanation: Four carbon atoms can be arranged in only two distinct ways: a straight chain of four, which is butane, and a chain of three with a methyl branch on the middle carbon, which is 2-methylpropane. Putting the branch on an end carbon simply recreates the straight chain.

distractorRationale.a: Only counting the straight chain misses the branched arrangement
distractorRationale.c: Three isomers is the count for pentane, C5H12
distractorRationale.d: Putting the methyl group on carbon 1 or carbon 3 gives the same molecule as butane, so those are not new isomers

questions.stem: Methane reacts with chlorine in the presence of ultraviolet light. The type of reaction and one of the products are

options.text: neutralisation, giving a salt and water

questions.explanation: Methane is saturated, so nothing can be added to it. Ultraviolet light splits chlorine molecules into radicals, which replace hydrogen atoms one at a time: CH4 + Cl2 -> CH3Cl + HCl. In the dark no reaction occurs at all.

distractorRationale.a: Addition requires a double or triple bond, and CH4Cl2 would give carbon five bonds
distractorRationale.c: Polymerisation requires unsaturated monomers such as ethene
distractorRationale.d: There is no acid and no base involved, so neutralisation cannot apply

questions.stem: The boiling points of the alkanes increase steadily from methane to decane because as the chain lengthens

options.text: the C-C covalent bonds become stronger
the van der Waals forces between molecules become stronger
hydrogen bonding develops between the molecules

questions.explanation: Boiling separates molecules from one another, so it is the intermolecular forces that matter. Longer alkane molecules have more electrons and a larger surface of contact, which produces stronger temporary dipoles and therefore stronger van der Waals attraction requiring more energy to overcome.

distractorRationale.a: The C-C bonds inside the molecule are not broken during boiling
distractorRationale.c: Hydrogen bonding needs hydrogen attached to F, O or N, none of which is present in an alkane
distractorRationale.d: Alkanes are essentially non-polar regardless of chain length

questions.stem: A generator running in a poorly ventilated room is dangerous mainly because incomplete combustion of the fuel produces
questions.explanation: With a limited oxygen supply, hydrocarbons burn incompletely to give carbon monoxide instead of carbon dioxide. Carbon monoxide is colourless and odourless and binds to haemoglobin roughly 200 times more strongly than oxygen, so it starves the body of oxygen without any warning.

distractorRationale.a: Carbon dioxide comes from complete combustion and is far less toxic at the concentrations involved
distractorRationale.c: Water vapour is produced in both complete and incomplete combustion and is harmless
distractorRationale.d: Hydrogen gas is not a product of hydrocarbon combustion

questions.stem: What is the IUPAC name of the compound CH3-CH(CH3)-CH2-CH3?
questions.explanation: The longest continuous chain contains four carbons, so the parent is butane, and a single methyl group is attached. Numbering from the end that gives the branch the lower locant places it on carbon 2, giving 2-methylbutane.

distractorRationale.b: The chain was numbered from the wrong end; IUPAC rules require the lowest possible locant
distractorRationale.c: This name has only a three-carbon parent chain, so it corresponds to C4H10 rather than C5H12
distractorRationale.d: Pentane is the unbranched five-carbon isomer, a different compound
